summary: Implements bounded read-error reporting inside completion_inbox.py (no core.py/server.py change): every taskctl `list`/`show` call in _fetch_full_cards is now try/except-guarded so a raised exception degrades to a recorded error instead of crossing build_completion_inbox() uncaught, and the LIST call's returncode is now checked (previously only the SHOW call's returncode was checked) so a nonzero-returncode LIST failure with empty stdout is no longer indistinguishable from a genuinely empty queue. Both failure modes are surfaced via a new additive `read_errors` facet (scope: list|show, error_kind: nonzero_returncode|exception, bounded/truncated error_message) plus a `counts.read_errors` integer. The pre-existing `fetch_errors` facet (task_id + error, SHOW-scoped) keeps its exact original shape/contents for backward compatibility -- this closes blocker list_call_failure_silently_swallowed and blocker no_tool_error_event_kind_exists from the B279 next-wave file, scoped to the completion_inbox read layer only (no new geoai_completion_inbox_delta tool, no server.py change -- out of this task's allowed_writes).

context7_usage.reason: Pure repo-local implementation task inside an already-read local module (completion_inbox.py); no new external library/framework/API/CLI/service surface was touched. changes: New helper _result_fields(result) -- extracts (returncode, stdout, stderr) from a dict or attribute-bearing object without raising; used for both LIST and SHOW results (previously only SHOW had this dict-or-object handling inline).
_fetch_full_cards: LIST call now wrapped in try/except Exception -> read_errors entry {scope:list, status, topic, error_kind:exception, error_message} instead of propagating.

_fetch_full_cards: LIST result's returncode is now checked via _result_fields; nonzero -> read_errors entry {scope:list, status, topic, error_kind:nonzero_returncode, error_message} and rows=[] (bounded degrade, not a raw empty-queue read).
_fetch_full_cards: SHOW call now wrapped in try/except Exception -> fetch_errors entry (backward-compatible shape) AND read_errors entry {scope:show, task_id, error_kind:exception, error_message}.

_fetch_full_cards: SHOW nonzero returncode path (pre-existing) now ALSO appends a read_errors entry {scope:show, task_id, error_kind:nonzero_returncode, error_message} in addition to the unchanged fetch_errors entry.
_fetch_full_cards return signature widened from (cards, fetch_errors) to (cards, fetch_errors, read_errors) -- internal helper, single caller (build_completion_inbox) updated in the same file.

build_completion_inbox: collects read_errors across all three canonical statuses (pending/processing/review) and adds it as a new top-level additive facet plus counts.read_errors; every pre-existing top-level key (review_queue, stale_processing, runner_mismatch_warnings, latest_validation_facts, fetch_errors, counts.*, authority_flags, mutation) is unchanged in shape and content on the clean path.
Module + function docstrings updated to document the B280 bounded read-error contract; no change to READONLY/LAUNCH_IMPLEMENTED/SUBPROCESS_LAUNCH_TRIPWIRE module constants or _authority_flags().
implementation.facet_shape_compatibility: additive-only: existing fetch_errors/review_queue/stale_processing/runner_mismatch_warnings/latest_validation_facts/counts keys and value shapes are byte-identical to pre-B280 behavior on the clean (no read-tool-failure) path; read_errors and counts.read_errors are the only new keys.

neural_bridge_note: No learned decision authority and no regex/keyword cue router introduced. The changed code (_fetch_full_cards try/except + returncode checks) is pure deterministic error-boundary/evidence-bounding logic on an existing read-only tool-shelling layer -- it decides nothing about task content, routing, or intelligence; it only prevents an already-existing read-source failure mode from silently mispresenting as an empty result or crashing the calling process. Not applicable to neural_bridge_priority's applies_to list (translation/routing/toolisa/coding/stem/context_graph/shared_axis/open_generation) -- this is task_mcp infrastructure reliability, not a learnable capability.
